causal.assumptions_right: USD rates advantage versus CAD was real and funded the harvested win. USDCAD spot was the clean expression of that gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Treated leftover size as inexpensive peak-recapture optionality and underweighted three-digit oil as a CAD impulse that can stall USDCAD even with a 168bp front-end gap.
causal.causal_divergence: Core P&L came from harvesting the rates-gap trade. Residual risk was a 1.40/1.40 round trip because what remained was oil-and-event inventory, not the original rates gap.
causal.future_implication: Harvest-to-flat is mandatory on USDCAD after a material win when oil is three-digit. No reopen at 1.4028 this dual-CB week.
causal.observed_reality: Oil printed three-digit and is still there (WTI 101.76, Brent 115.81), Canadian impulse rose, and the leftover exited at the same 1.40 it was opened at, with Fed and BoC immediately ahead.
causal.original_belief: The SOFR-CORRA and UST-CAN 10Y gap would keep USDCAD bid, so a smaller leftover could recapture the prior peak without needing full size.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Going fully flat when oil went three-digit and CAD impulse rose would have kept the realized win and avoided carrying remnant risk into Fed and BoC.

items.expression_assessment: Spot USDCAD was the right pair: both legs visible, no extra EUR or oil-beta cross. Expression was not the error.

facts.invalidation: Fed path recast as one-and-done and/or BoC/energy re-tightens CAD enough to close the policy gap.

items.future_rule: Do not leave a reduced USDCAD leftover waiting on peak recapture when oil is three-digit. Re-enter only if the desk would initiate from flat at the live print, and not into dual Fed/BoC week.
items.lesson: After a material USDCAD harvest, three-digit oil plus rising Canadian impulse means flatten fully.
items.sizing_assessment: Cutting down after the win was correct; not cutting to zero was the miss. Reduced leftover is not a free call on peak recapture.
items.thesis_assessment: Long USD versus CAD on the policy-rate and 10Y gap was directionally right and is why the trade paid. That thesis did not license leftover inventory once oil became a CAD impulse.
items.timing_assessment: The 19 Sep entry caught the rates gap. Holding the remnant into three-digit oil and the 28 Oct dual sitting was late. Exit at 1.40 closed the leftover without giving back the harvested core.
items.what_failed: A reduced leftover was left on to recapture a prior peak. It round-tripped 1.40 to 1.40 over about 36 days while oil went three-digit and Canadian impulse rose into Fed/BoC week.
items.what_worked: The USD-CAD rates gap paid. Expressing it in USDCAD spot, not a cross, let the core be harvested for a material realized gain.
